title: fix(core): refuse an empty operator map that is all a filter says (objectui#9164)
body:
Fixes #9164
Clause-②: no

## What changed

- `convertFiltersToAST` (`packages/core/src/utils/filter-converter.ts`). The loop records the first field whose value is an operator map with NO operators. The general tail refuses it through a new `refuseEmptyOperatorMap`: a `FilterOperatorError` (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400) with `field` set and no `operator`, whose message names the field and the fix (choose an operator, or remove the key). The refusal sits after the objectui#8770 / objectui#9030 identity fold and the objectui#9020 all-skipped guard, just before `return filter`. That line now serves only `{}`.
- Scope is the tail, as ruled: the empty operator map is refused only when nothing else in the filter produced a condition. `{ a: {} }`, `{ a: {}, b: undefined }` and `{ $and: [], a: {} }` are refused. `{}` and `{ a: 'x' }` keep their answers.
- One consequence of refusing in the shared tail: a combinator child that is an empty operator map is refused too. `{ $or: [{ a: {} }, { b: 2 }] }` used to lower to `undefined` (every row), because `lowerLogicalGroup` read the child's returned object as a TRUE disjunct.
- Docblocks brought in line: `FilterRefusalSubject`, `filterRefusalSubject`, `isOperatorMap`, the `lowerLogicalGroup` child comment, and the `@throws` / `@example` of `convertFiltersToAST`.
- Tests: new `filter-empty-operator-map-9164.test.ts`. The boundary rows in the sibling files that pinned the object coming back now pin the refusal: core 8770, 9020, 9030, 9001, 8567, and data-objectstack 9020. The objectui#9050 throw-site enumeration gains its row.
- Changesets: `.changeset/9164-empty-operator-map-refused.md` (`'@object-ui/core': patch`). The pending entries this makes false carry a dated note in the objectui#10533 form, with their frontmatter byte-identical (checked by md5 before and after): 8770, 8567, 8555 and 9050.

## H1 — census: who can emit an empty operator map

| producer | emits `{ field: {} }` on a live path? | evidence |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `FilterConditionField` `condToMongo` (sharing-rule criteria builder) | no | A throwaway probe drove the real `condToMongo`, `groupToCondition` and `buildFilterCondition` over every operator id, blank value shape and field type, 3888 calls in all, then JSON round-tripped the output as storage does. It is not committed. Hits came only from comparison operators with value `undefined`: `{ f: { $gt: undefined } }` is stored as `{"f":{}}`. The builder never holds `undefined` there. `addCondition` seeds `""`, `reshapeFilterValue` answers `""` for a scalar operator, and `LookupValuePicker` clears to `""`. Its output is written to `criteria_json`, which the server evaluates; no objectui path lowers it through this converter. An unfilled `between` has returned `null` since objectui#9914. |
| dataset filter inspector `groupToCondition` | no | probe: 0 hits. Every part is `{ [mop]: v }` or a copy of a non-empty valueless map. |
| dashboard `buildFilterCondition` | no | `if (!from && !to) return undefined`; `isEmptyValue` catches `{}`. The probe's hits for `{ from: undefined, to: undefined }` on select / lookup / number come from its own JSON round-trip. At runtime that object has two keys and fails as an unknown operator, and these conditions are never stored. |
| view config (`ListViewSchema.filter`, `ViewTab.filter`) | no | spec `ViewFilterRule[]`, lowered by `viewFilterRuleToNode`; never the `$` dialect |
| URL filter params (`parseUrlFilterTriples`) | no | the read side emits triples |
| ListView filter panel, user filters, quick filters | no | `FilterGroup` goes through `convertFilterGroupToAST` to AST triples |
| placeholder resolvers (`resolveFilterPlaceholders`) | no (was yes) | they used to rebuild a `Date` into `{}` until objectui#10506; both walkers keep every key |
| dataset drill (`buildDatasetDrillFilter`) | no | `{ $gte: r.gte, $lt: r.lt }` always has two keys at runtime |
| `RecordPickerDialog` `lookupFiltersToRecord` / `filterValuesToRecord` | only from authored metadata | `eq` passes the authored value through, so `{}` needs an author to write it |
| authored metadata (`table.defaultFilters`, page `config.filter`, lookup filters) | only if written | the case this refusal is for |

No live path answers yes, so the stop valve did not fire.

## H2 — where the refusal lands

| caller | entry | what the user sees for `{ a: {} }` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectGrid` `schema.filter` (render `useMemo`) | `toFilterNodeSafely` | the malformed-filter state, subject `a` |
| `RelatedList` scope filter (render `useMemo`) | `toFilterNodeSafely` | the malformed-filter state, subject `a` |
| `LineItemsPanel` scope filter (render `useMemo`) | `toFilterNodeSafely` | the malformed-filter state, subject `a` |
| `ValueDataSource.find` | `toFilterNodeSafely`, ARRAY `$filter` only | not reached: an object `$filter` goes to its own matcher, which this change does not touch |
| `ObjectGrid` deprecated `defaultFilters` leg | `toFilterNode`, inside the load `try` | `setError`; the malformed branch names the subject |
| `plugin-list` `buildEffectiveFilter` (ListView load and export) | `mergeFilterNodes`, inside the load `try` | a failed load that `classifyLoadError` reads as a malformed filter |
| `plugin-view` `ObjectView` | `mergeFilterNodes`, inside `try` | a failed load |
| `@object-ui/data-objectstack` `find()` (both routes) and export | `convertFiltersToAST` / `translateFilterToAST` inside `async` | a rejected promise with the envelope, and no request sent. Before, the plain route sent `?a=[object Object]` and the `$expand` route sent `filter={"a":{}}`. |
| `LookupField` recent rows | `mergeFilterNodes` inside an `async` `try` | the recent list stays empty |
| `related-count-store` `fetchCount` | `mergeFilterNodes` in an `async` function | a rejected count |
| `PeoplePicker` `recentFilter`, `RecordPickerDialog` `mergedFilter`, `composeElementDataSource` (via `useElementDataSource`), `composeDrillFilter` | `mergeFilterNodes`, at render or at click time | These throw for every refusal this converter raises, not only this one. objectui#9050 converted three render-time readers and not these. They are reachable with `{ a: {} }` only from authored metadata, because H1 found no producer. Read, not measured: see Acceptance notes. |

## Pins and ablation

The three refusal rows assert the envelope (`FilterOperatorError`, `code` `INVALID_FILTER`, `httpStatus` 400, `field` `a`, no `operator`, `filterRefusalSubject` `a`). They do not rely on `toThrow()` alone, and the message is not pinned.

- **Red on base.** The base converter (`17b323e5c`) was swapped into the tree, the blob hash verified equal to base, and 9 files run. Result: `Tests  17 failed | 165 passed (182)`. The red rows are the 3 ruled refusal rows, the safe-entry row, the 2 nested-child rows, the 9 updated boundary rows, and the objectui#9050 subject row plus its throw-site count. The controls stay green: `{}` / `toFilterNode({})`, `{ a: 'x' }`, the TRUE-identity and all-skipped members, and the whole objectui#8555 file. The trap restored the file: `RESTORED hash=084c1d1a1c08… == HEAD blob; git diff HEAD empty`.
- **Green on head.** At `ec8bf218ab`, `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/` plus seven data-objectstack and script filter tests gave `Test Files  183 passed (183)`, `Tests  3696 passed (3696)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- **Ablation** (`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, from the objectstack checkout). It deleted `if (emptyOperatorMapField !== undefined) refuseEmptyOperatorMap(emptyOperatorMapField);`. Proof it landed: `anchor x1 -> x0`, `blob 084c1d1a1c08 -> 906bff2c0cc6`. The same 9 files gave `Tests  16 failed | 166 passed (182)`. The red rows are every row that asserts a refusal: the 3 ruled rows, the safe-entry row, the 2 nested rows, the 9 boundary rows and the objectui#9050 subject row. No control went red. The throw-site count stays green because the throw site remains. Restore proof: `blob == HEAD (084c1d1a1c08) and git diff HEAD is empty`. The subject resolves to `src` through the root vitest alias (`@object-ui/core` maps to `packages/core/src`), so no `dist` rebuild takes part.
- ⚠️ The dispatch predicted the ablation would redden exactly three rows. It reddened 16. The other 13 all assert the same refusal, on the safe entry, the nested children, the sibling files' boundary rows and the enumeration.

## Gates (HEAD `ec8bf218ab`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check` runs `tsc --noEmit` and then `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: `TYPECHECK_EXIT=0`. `--listFiles` on the test program contains all 7 edited or new core test files. The dependency closure was built first with `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/core^...' build`.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/data-objectstack^...' build` followed by `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack type-check`, whose program includes its tests: `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: `✅  9 source file(s) of 2 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: `✅  No changeset declares a major bump`.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` is report-only. It lists the 4 dated-note edits, and each one's declaration at base equals its declaration now.
- `pnpm check:changeset-claims`: `✅  No pending changeset names a file this change touches`.
- `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` ✅, `pnpm check:control-bytes` ✅ (`OK (scanned 8966 tracked text file(s)`), `pnpm check:test-path-roots` ✅.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s)`.
- Lint, narrowed to the 9 touched `.ts` files with `pnpm exec eslint --format json`:
  - Result: `files_linted=9 errors=0 warnings=17`. All 17 warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any`, and the diff adds zero `any` tokens.
  - Population: eslint's own JSON reports 9 results and no ignored-file notice.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`, and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the disk. So this diff cannot move the verdict of an untouched file.
- NOT MEASURED: the repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test`. Both belong to CI.

## Serial

`git fetch origin main` into a private ref, then `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD` against `bf14b64608`: exit 0, tree `5b6db2b4ca`. Five commits landed on `main` after the base, and none touches a file in this diff. The open-PR file lists were not re-read; the PM read them at 13:30Z.

## Acceptance notes

- **The sibling boundary still widens.** `{ status: 'a', created: {} }` still lowers to `['status', '=', 'a']`: an empty operator map beside a key that lowers is dropped. objectui#8555 and objectui#8567 pin that on purpose. The ruling scoped this card to the tail, so this PR does not move it. `@objectstack/spec` records `{ field: {} }` as REJECTED by objectstack#5240 in every position, so the report hands it to the seat as a class (b) finding.
- **Reading of "8770 / 9020 / 9030's members and pins stay as they are".** Their members' pins are byte-unchanged. Their boundary rows pinned THIS card's three inputs coming back as the object, and the ruling requires those inputs refused. Those rows now pin the refusal, keep their fence ("no fold claims it"), and carry an UPDATED note.
- **The invariant "undefined or an AST".** It now holds for every return except `{}` itself. The ruling keeps `{}` as a control, and `toFilterNode` folds it one level up.
- **Render-time throwers.** `PeoplePicker` `recentFilter`, `RecordPickerDialog` `mergedFilter`, `composeElementDataSource` and `composeDrillFilter` throw for every converter refusal. This is read from the code, not measured. The class predates this change.
- **Dormant producer.** `condToMongo` emits an empty map only for a comparison row whose value is `undefined`, and the builder never produces that today.
- **Changesets left alone.** The 8513 changeset's "Why this is a fix" paragraph says the converter returns the original object for the TRUE identities. That has been false since objectui#8770, not because of this change, so it was left. The 8770 changeset's all-null half had already been answered by objectui#9020, and the dated note says so.
- **Historical count.** The objectui#8567 test header's "seven throws" is a count from that change and was left alone.
